# Contract-First

Curated by Skill Harbor: a collaboration method for coordinating frontend/backend or service-to-service work through one authoritative, machine-checkable contract (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Protocol Buffers, or JSON Schema). Consumers state what they need, providers implement that shape, and both sides verify against the same artifact before integration, so parallel work can evolve an API or event schema without field drift, mock/production shape mismatch, or one side silently redefining the interface. It governs how teams change a boundary: when field names, nullability, enums, or error shapes start drifting, when mocks no longer match production, or when a provider change can break consumers maintained by someone else. It complements API design guidance (what a good API looks like) and regression testing (guarding fixed bugs from returning). By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure method, nothing to install; do not add contract machinery to a tiny single-module boundary that one person changes alone, the overhead is not worth it there. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
